summary: The expand_col, backfill_data, and sync_trigger stages passed with 0 failures. deploy_new then failed 22 consistency checks: reads returned seed-level or null data instead of expected values, and 22 rows showed column disagreement between note and customer_note. retire_old succeeded, but contract_col was skipped due to the 22 earlier failures.
revision_notes: The note_sync_trigger fails under concurrent interleaved writes from both app versions; its bidirectional sync logic produces incorrect results when OLD is NULL (new-version inserts) or when versions interleave, causing reads to return seed-level/null data and 22 rows to mismatch between note and customer_note columns.

stages.description: Add new column customer_note on the account_user table.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into the new column.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Create a trigger that synchronizes note and customer_note on INSERT or UPDATE.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER note_sync_trigger AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new version that only knows the customer_note column. The migration is state_only.
The old version is taken offline; no further writes to the note column will occur.
Remove the note column and its trigger after the old version is retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
